headline: Application role gains unrestricted read/write access to all S3 buckets instead of one specific bucket
suppressed: The stated intent to avoid paging when new buckets are added is understandable, but granting wildcard access is the wrong solution. Use a resource pattern like arn:aws:s3:::acme-prod-*, an S3 resource tag condition, or a process to manage the list instead.

findings.evidence_ref: aws_iam_role_policy.app_data policy Resource field changes from ["arn:aws:s3:::acme-prod-data", "arn:aws:s3:::acme-prod-data/*"] to ["*"] in terraform plan
findings.explanation: The application's IAM policy now grants s3:GetObject, s3:PutObject, and s3:ListBucket permissions on all S3 resources in the account, instead of being limited to the acme-prod-data bucket. This violates least privilege and allows the app to read, modify, and list any bucket.
